decisions.reason: A same-message MODIFY already records that the Hero V establishes the complete architectural language for the remaining proprietary alphabet.
The source does not change the second V's geometry or Hero-V derivation; its hierarchy clarification belongs to the separate visual-hierarchy Requirement and restates an existing rule.
The requirement already specifies that the second V sits slightly above E and L, below the Hero V and É accent, and acts as a quiet non-competing echo; the source adds no new state.
The source mentions the Hero V and É accent only as the existing upper boundary for the second V and does not change their peak-alignment rule.
A same-message MODIFY already captures the request to explain how the architectural principles are translated into rendered letterforms.
Clarifying that the Hero V governs more than stroke weight and terminal details broadens the E/L architectural basis but does not alter the established shared-terminal treatment.
The source does not change the requirement that the É accent reuse the literal Hero V terminal geometry.
The proprietary-alphabet clarification concerns letterform design language and does not establish any change to spacing or kerning.
The source changes neither the deferred material treatment nor its role in enhancing the resolved geometry.
The architectural letterform clarification is unrelated to proof-file formats or Mac viewability.
